children: The energy sector
advanced nearly 12% in the month of October, compared to a 1.1% fall in the broader market (
The move was driven largely by war-related supply disruptions and a steep rise in crude oil and refined product prices. Crude oil (

) climbed to its highest level in more than six months as escalating tensions in the Middle East heightened concerns over potential supply disruptions. Brent crude briefly surpassed $117 a barrel to reach its highest level since April.
Energy Sector Scorecard
Sector Return: +11.67%
Best Performer: APA (+21.87%)
Worst Performer: Valero Energy (-2.15%)
Top Theme: Geopolitical uncertainty

"The month featured several events that boosted oil and oil product prices, such as new attacks on ships in the Persian Gulf, a drop in traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, and greater risks of a new United States offensive against Iran," explained Seeking Alpha analyst
Top energy performers of the month
On the individual front, APA
was the biggest winner in October, gaining nearly 22%. It was followed by ConocoPhillips
, which gained 21.2% in the last month.
"APA and ConocoPhillips are pure oil companies, so they are much more sensitive to oil prices. APA had 17 analysts raising expectations for the results versus just 4 reducing expectations".

"ConocoPhillips had 20 analysts raising earnings expectations versus just 4 lowering expectations. Therefore, the strong rise in the shares of these two companies embodies strong expectations of improved results due to high oil prices," the analyst added.

Top energy detractor of the month
On the other hand, Valero Energy
was the biggest detractor in October, slipping 2.15% in the month, followed by Texas Pacific Land
that lost 1.42%.

"Valero Energy and Texas Pacific were the main detractors, falling 2.15% and 1.42%, respectively. The big highlight here is Valero Energy. The company is one of the largest independent refiners in the USA; therefore, the release of strategic reserves from Europe and relief from Russian sanctions were negatively impacted. Not to mention that investors may have priced in the peak of the cycle, with lower spreads ahead," Multiplo Invest noted.
